the physicochemical profile of the carboxyl acid moiety is difficult to replace, but that the use of isosteres may be a useful strategy to achieve a desired physicochemical profile.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

isosteric replacements for carboxylic acids are generally tolerated with regard to physicochemical properties; however, there is a clear trend that isosteres that maintain the hydrogen bond acceptor (HBA) and hydrogen bond donor (HBD) features of the caroxylate group tend to be more favorable.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the physicochemical profile of carboxyic acid isosteres is largely dependent on the electronic nature of the replacement, rather than the steric bulk.
the isosteric replacements are generally well tolerated, with the exception of the sulfonic acid and the sulfonyl fluoride analogs.

the carboxyamide, carboxyurea, and carboxylate groups are the most suitable replacements for the carboxy moiety, with minimal perturbation to the properties that the carboxylate group confers to the parent molecule, and with a minimal impact on the physiochemical properties of the molecule.
